fieldsRead.text: American Studies is Radboud’s English-taught specialisation within the BA English Language and Culture. It studies the United States through history, politics, literature, media, culture and language, with English proficiency, a thesis and substantial minor and elective space.

Three related UCR programmes emphasise society and politics, cultural interpretation, or political institutions and global affairs. All include American-focused study, alongside broader comparative courses. They provide less dedicated American literature and English-language training than Radboud, and the scheduled courses do not replace its separate bachelor thesis.

Radboud labels this prospective 2027-intake pathway provisional and subject to change. Year 2 requires two 15 EC Faculty of Arts minors; year 3 retains 30 EC of genuine elective space. RADAr and mentoring are additional zero-credit obligations. The published first-year continuation threshold is 45 of 60 EC, subject to personal circumstances. The optional Dutch-taught educational minor has separate teaching-qualification conditions.

Two 15 EC Faculty of Arts minors, one per semester. Each own-programme additional minor selects three 5 EC courses from its relevant menu; other Faculty language/culture or interdisciplinary minors are also allowed.
A required 10-EC bachelor thesis completes independent work in American Studies.

30 EC genuine elective space, normally 15 EC per semester on the home-study route. Internship or an optional Dutch-taught educational minor may fill this space. Study abroad uses a different listed third-year pathway.

Radboud provides a dedicated American Studies sequence in United States history, politics, literature, media and cultural memory, alongside English linguistics, language proficiency and a required thesis. UCR offers American-focused gender and Indigenous history, historical research, media and race, supported by comparative politics, literature, law and social inquiry. Its broader comparative courses do not reproduce the full specialist sequence, English phonetics or American-literature survey. Its scheduled historical seminar develops source-based research and a substantial paper; optional independent research remains separate from the 24-course programme.

American-focused history and media combine with comparative politics, international relations, sociology, literature, art and rhetoric. Qualitative inquiry, historical research concerning the American Century and psycholinguistics supply complementary research and language perspectives.

Literature, film, media, art and creative communication organise this cultural route, with American gender history, mainstream media and race providing a substantial United States focus. Comparative literary study and environmental media broaden its interpretive methods.

American-focused history, media and race combine with comparative government, political thought, rights, law and international relations. Civil-society theory, environmental-justice movements and youth-radicalisation research provide specific comparative perspectives on power and social conflict.
